digests.title: TLDR Daily Digest
digests.tagline: Tech, AI, IT, Web Dev, InfoSec, DevOps, Design, Data

stories.headline: Stripe Nears $7 Billion Acquisition of AI Router OpenRouter
stories.blurb: Stripe is reportedly finalizing a deal to acquire AI model-routing platform OpenRouter for over $7 billion, signaling a massive bet on helping developers optimize and switch between increasingly costly AI providers.

stories.headline: Anthropic Holds Back "Model 2" Due to Rising AI Risks
stories.blurb: Anthropic has chosen not to release an internal model more powerful than Mythos as it signals growing difficulty in understanding the rapidly accelerating capabilities and risks of its own systems.

stories.headline: Nvidia Slashes Financial Guarantee for OpenAI Data Center Campus
stories.blurb: Nvidia cut its financial backstop for OpenAI's planned massive Ohio data center from $250 billion to under $120 billion to address investor concerns over its chipmaking risk exposure.

stories.headline: OpenAI Exercises Warrants for $2.3B Cerebras Stake Ahead of Ultrafast Launch
stories.blurb: OpenAI spent just $100 to acquire a 4.2% stake in hardware maker Cerebras right before previewing its "Ultrafast" high-speed tier, making Cerebras' specialized chips the backbone of its fastest model offerings.

stories.headline: Z.ai Releases GLM-5.3 With Advanced Coding and Cybersecurity Capabilities
stories.blurb: China's Z.ai has launched GLM-5.3, a model showing significant jumps in complex coding and vulnerability exploitation through scaled post-training, though its model weights are being delayed due to safety checks.

stories.headline: White House Approves Private "Hack-Back" Operations Against Cybercriminals
stories.blurb: A new U.S. program authorizes vetted private companies to launch disruptive, government-approved cyberattacks to dismantle systems and data controlled by foreign cybercrime syndicates.

stories.headline: Near-Autonomous AI Attack Targets Taiwanese Government Systems
stories.blurb: Threat actors deployed open-source AI frameworks to run self-directed "Learning Cycles" that adapted to failures, marking the first known near-autonomous AI cyberattack targeting government personnel records.

stories.headline: Brave Browser Combats GPU Fingerprinting With WebGL "Farbling"
stories.blurb: Brave version 1.93 introduces default protections that randomize highly identifying WebGL and WebGPU hardware signals, neutralizing advanced cross-site tracking without breaking web graphics.

stories.headline: Amazon Reshapes AWS Architecture to Battle the Power Crunch
stories.blurb: Under an internal initiative called "Region Flex," Amazon is migrating over 100 software workloads to bypass severe electricity and data center constraints in major AWS hubs.

stories.headline: Tailscale Squashes a 16-Year-Old SQLite Corruption Bug
stories.blurb: Tailscale engineers spent six months tracing a rare database corruption issue to a 16-year-old race condition in SQLite's WAL checkpointing, prompting an official upstream fix.

stories.headline: Why AI Models Are Getting Dumber on Purpose
stories.blurb: Modern AI models are intentionally shedding raw factual recall to prioritize cheaper, faster reasoning, relying instead on real-time external data retrieval to reduce hallucinations and remain current.

stories.headline: The Imminent "TEMU-fication" of Software and Digital Services
stories.blurb: The rapid rise of cheap, AI-generated software threatens to flood the digital landscape with low-quality products, creating a two-tier market where human-crafted software becomes a premium luxury.

stories.headline: Rethinking the UX Team's Role in the Era of Ubiquitous AI
stories.blurb: As AI tools democratize interface creation across organizations, UX teams must pivot from hands-on production to building design systems, playbooks, and standards that guide wider output.
